DETERMINATION
The observation-cursor behaviour that applies to this integration is the Ordarium 1.3.1 incremental state-change-feed cursor — spec ORD-BOOT-0 as refined by ORD-BOOT-0.1 (global high-water validation). The 1.2.0-line behaviour asserted in docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md ("has no notion of a change-feed cursor and no cursor-invalidation failure") does NOT apply to this workspace.

WHY (provenance / version scope — resolved locally)
- Load-bearing dependency sources agree on 1.3.1: package.json:32-37 pins @ordarium/{core,host-kit,ledger-sqlite,testing} to the ordarium-v1.3.1 GitHub release tarballs; pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18 repeats the same four overrides; the installed artifacts node_modules/@ordarium/{core,host-kit,ledger-sqlite}/package.json all report version 1.3.1. src/effects/runtime.ts builds `new SqliteLedger(...)`, `new OrdariumRuntime(...)` and `createStateStore({runtime})` from exactly those packages, so the running integration is on 1.3.1.
- The conflicting sources are explicitly non-load-bearing. docs/release-commentary-1.2.0.md self-scopes and self-supersedes: "describes the state at the 1.2.0 release line ... Anything here applies only to the 1.2.0 line. Status: historical, superseded by later releases." README.md:26 still links ordarium-v1.0.0 and lists only three deps — host-kit (which Palimpsest added at 1.2.0) is absent — so it is stale install text. docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md is a revision log whose newest logged baseline is 1.2.0; per its own §3.1 the pin lines are the object that gets bumped, and no 1.3.1 bump has been logged there. So the only conflict is stale documentation vs manifest+installed artifact, and version scope/supersession settles it. No genuine unresolved conflict remains, so no peer round-trip is warranted.
- Corroborating drift: test/ordarium_ledger.test.ts:124,154 still asserts Ordarium PRAGMA user_version = 3, while the pinned 1.3.1 ledger sets LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION = 4 (migrations.js). The repo's own tests/docs lag the manifest, not the reverse.

THE APPLICABLE BEHAVIOUR (from the pinned artifacts)
1. Capability-gated feed: LedgerCapabilities.stateChangeFeed = true; OrdariumStateStore.changes(filter?, cursor?); supportsStateChangeFeed() is the fail-closed entry — a ledger without the capability throws LEDGER_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED (core/dist/src/state.{js,d.ts}, types.d.ts).
2. Cursor is opaque: base64url of {"c":"<digits>"}, decoding to a non-negative safe integer.
3. Durable, global, filter-independent commit-observation position over the ordering table (change_seq), ascending. Unlike the other read surfaces' optional `nextCursor`, StateChangePage.cursor is always present — at end of feed too — so a consumer keeps a durable resume position; `hasMore` signals matching changes beyond the page. Default page 100, ceiling RESOURCE_LIMITS.maxStateChangePageItems = 1000.
4. Fail-closed invalidation (ORD-BOOT-0.1): an undecodable cursor, or a position greater than the ledger's global high-water mark (MAX(change_seq)), throws InvalidCursorError with code INVALID_CURSOR — invalid caller input, distinct from LEDGER_CORRUPT, and it never silently restarts from the beginning of the feed. Validation is against the whole ledger, not the requested namespace; concurrent commits only raise the mark so a valid cursor cannot be falsely rejected, while a restored/replaced/rewound ledger fails closed.
5. Atomicity: the ordering row is inserted in the same transaction as the state-revision CAS, so a committed revision and its observable position are never split and a rolled-back CAS leaves neither.
6. Migration: v3→v4 backfills existing revisions with deterministic synthetic positions in (namespace,key,revision) order, explicitly labelled migration order rather than original commit order; post-v4 commits carry the real durable DB order. Relevant because Palimpsest keeps durable shared ledgers under $DSH_HOME.

SCOPE NUANCE
Palimpsest's own code currently exercises only the state list/CAS surface, not the feed: src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts:64-71 loads telemetry via OrdariumStateStore.list(...) using the per-subject {s}/nextCursor pagination, and grep finds no calls to changes()/supportsStateChangeFeed()/INVALID_CURSOR. So the observation (change-feed) cursor is exposed by the pinned ledger and governs whenever the integration observes the feed; it is not the per-subject list cursor, and it is unrelated to Palimpsest's internal /api/graph EventCursor vs ViewCursor (docs/engineering/35, a separate axis).

CONCLUSION
Applicable: Ordarium 1.3.1 ORD-BOOT-0 / ORD-BOOT-0.1 state-change-feed observation cursor (opaque {"c"} position, always-present durable resume point, global filter-independent high-water validation, fail-closed INVALID_CURSOR). Inapplicable: the 1.2.0-line commentary behaviour, which is explicitly historical and superseded, and the v1.0.0 README link, which is stale doc drift contradicted by package.json, pnpm-workspace.yaml and the installed 1.3.1 artifacts.
